channel.title: nexusEVnews
channel.description: Independent EV and renewable energy news, curated daily. Electric vehicles, solar, battery tech, and charging infrastructure.

item.title: Infinite Machine's Alto Wants to Fill the Gap Between an E-Bike and a Vespa
item.dc:creator: InsideEVs
item.description: A New York startup built a class-3 electric scooter that needs no plates and no insurance in most states. It does 28 mph, has full suspension and a removable 1.2 kWh battery, and a GPS chip that keeps transmitting even after you pull the battery out. InsideEVs spent a week riding it around Manhattan, including leaving it outside for five days.

item.title: Hammond Drove the NIO ES9 Around Shanghai. The Suspension Was What Surprised Him Most.
item.dc:creator: Everything Electric APAC
item.description: NIO puts tiny hydraulic pumps directly at each wheel rather than routing pressure from a central unit. On Belgian paving stones at speed, the only evidence you're on them is the sound. A crowdsourced pothole database shared across every NIO vehicle pre-arms the suspension before the rough surface arrives.

item.title: The PV5 Starts at £31,495 After the UK EV Grant. The ID.Buzz Starts at £60,000. Electrifying Drove Both.
item.dc:creator: Electrifying
item.description: More boot space, a V2L socket, regen paddles, and one-pedal driving at roughly half the price. Both reviewers chose the Kia. The Buzz wins on power, range, electric sliding doors, and cabin quality. Neither is a bad choice, but the £27,000 gap makes one of them much easier to justify.

item.title: CES 2026's Electric Micromobility Floor: From a 36-lb Carbon Scooter to a 94 mph Speed Machine
item.dc:creator: EV Tech Steven
item.description: EV Tech Steven covered 14 electric two-wheelers from the CES floor: the all-carbon Novos light bike at 80 mph and 100 units, the InMotion RS Pro at 94 mph with a dashboard worth using, the LivaQ eQuad with four hub motors and 200 miles of range, and a rideable carry-on suitcase with a built-in power bank.

item.title: Xiaomi Hired Engineers From BMW, Porsche, and Lamborghini. EU Entry Is Second Half 2027.
item.dc:creator: Out of Spec Roaming
item.description: Fifty engineers in a Munich R&D centre. One ran the BMW M4 GT3 race programme. One tuned the 3 Series, Z4, and X5 chassis. One designed the exterior of the Porsche 992 GT3 RS. Another led the AMG Vision GT. Xiaomi has delivered over 400,000 vehicles and is targeting half a million in 2026.

item.title: The BMW iX3 Gets to Yorkshire First, But the Tesla Costs a Third Less to Charge
item.dc:creator: What Car?
item.description: What Car? drives the BMW iX3 and Tesla Model Y on a 500-mile London-to-Yorkshire round trip. The iX3 arrived first, logged real-world range of around 393 miles, and averaged 170 kW charging. The Tesla charged at 129 kW on average and cost £36 less to run over the full trip on Supercharger pricing.

item.title: Six More Inches, a Drain Plug, and a Tow Hitch: Why Most Buyers Land on the Model Y
item.dc:creator: Gjeebs
item.description: A dual owner of the Tesla Model 3 and Model Y compares both cars in detail. The premium variants are $42 apart per month on a 60-month loan. The Model Y adds six inches of rear legroom, 8 more cubic feet of cargo space, a frunk drain plug, and a tow hitch the Model 3 cannot have. Range difference: six miles.

item.title: Two Million EVs in the UK, the Renault 5 Is Outselling Everything, and the Corsa GSE Looks Like Trouble
item.dc:creator: Electrifying
item.description: The UK crossed 2 million EVs with April registrations up almost 60% year-on-year. The Renault 5 was April's bestselling EV at £230 per month. The Vauxhall Corsa GSE brings 281 hp and a limited-slip differential. CATL announced a semi-solid-state battery rated at 930 miles on the Chinese test cycle.

item.title: A Week With the Vauxhall Corsa Electric: It Drives Like a Corsa, and That's the Whole Point
item.dc:creator: Andrew Till / Mr. EV
item.description: Andrew Till spends a week with the Vauxhall Corsa Electric GS at £29,740, covering daily use, a Southampton round trip, and a rapid charge. Real-world efficiency was around 4 miles per kWh. The sat nav cannot plan charge stops without a paid third-party app, which matters on a 221-mile car.

item.title: CATL's CTO Says Solid State Is Still Years From Mass Production, and the BMW iX3 Surprised Even BMW
item.dc:creator: Everything Electric TECH
item.description: Everything Electric interviews CATL's overseas CTO at the 2026 Beijing Motor Show. The flash-charging Shenxing cell hits 10-80% in 3 minutes 44 seconds but requires 1,500 kW infrastructure. Solid-state demo cars are 1-2 years away; mass production is further out. BMW iX3 demand exceeded BMW's own internal forecasts.

item.title: The Gap Between the Spec Sheet and the Road Trip
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: Today's five stories tell the same story from different angles: EV hardware is advancing faster than the ecosystem around it. The cars are getting longer range, faster charging, and more performance. The charging networks, navigation software, and pricing structures haven't kept up. The thread that runs from CATL's lab through a Yorkshire road trip to a Kent supermarket car park.

item.title: The BMW iX Still Has Tricks the iX3 Can't Match, But the Price Gap Is Hard to Justify
item.dc:creator: Autogefühl
item.description: Thomas and Lea run the facelifted BMW iX on a full German Autobahn road trip. Real-world mixed range came in around 480 km, roughly 120 km behind the iX3 under the same conditions, and the 195 kW charging peak adds up to a 30-minute stop versus the iX3's 21 minutes.

item.title: Rivian's Spin-Off Built a 100-Mile E-Bike With No Chain and Automotive-Grade Ambitions
item.dc:creator: MotorTrend Channel
item.description: The Also TMB is a pedal-by-wire electric bike that spun out of Rivian, using Rivian R1 battery cells and a series-hybrid drivetrain with no mechanical chain. Starting at $3,500, it weighs 80 lbs, claims 100 miles of range, and tops out at 28 mph assisted.

item.title: You Know BYD Means Business When Daniel Craig Is Narrating the Ad
item.dc:creator: BYD Global
item.description: BYD's premium DENZA brand released a global brand film featuring Daniel Craig. No specs, no range figures, just a cinematic minute about change and new roads, signaling where BYD intends to compete next.

item.title: The $25,000 Electric Truck Made in Indiana That You're Allowed to Fix Yourself
item.dc:creator: Jay Leno's Garage
item.description: Jay Leno drives a prototype of the Slate truck, a modular electric pickup priced in the mid-$20,000s, built in Warsaw, Indiana. It has exposed fasteners, no paint, a composite body, and explicit right-to-repair support including DIY warranty repairs through a 4,000-shop independent service network.

item.title: A Quiet Forest Night With a BYD Sealion 7 and an Attached Tent: No Agenda
item.dc:creator: FISH13
item.description: A BYD Sealion 7 powers the Arbor Outdoor HEXONA tent for a quiet forest overnight with no talking and no range test. Vehicle-to-load EV camping done in a calm, ASMR style. Contains paid promotion for BYD Korea and Arbor Outdoor.

item.title: Two Batteries, One Hitch, and the Case for All-Electric Glamping
item.dc:creator: Jacob Hunka
item.description: The Lightship AE1 carries its own 69 kWh battery and 80 kW motor to neutralize trailer drag on the tow vehicle. Paired with a Rivian, the real-world efficiency numbers are hard to argue with. This is what all-electric glamping looks like when the hardware actually works.

item.title: Rivian Has an Uber Robotaxi Deal, a DoorDash Bot Spinoff, and Made the $20,000 VW ID.1 Possible
item.dc:creator: Munro Live
item.description: RJ Scaringe confirmed a deal with Uber to build a robotaxi on the R2 platform and described DoorDash delivery bots being built by Rivian spinoff ALSO. He also explained how the same zonal computing architecture behind the R1 and R2 let Volkswagen engineer the ID.1 at a roughly $20,000 price point.

item.title: Scout's Traveler and Terra Get a Style Refresh. The 2027 Production Target Hasn't Changed.
item.dc:creator: The Fast Lane Car
item.description: The Traveler wears a new matte white called White Cap with 20-inch wheels and 35-inch KO3 tires, and the brick-red interior is the most complete cabin look yet. Running and driving mules are in cold-weather testing in Europe. Production is still on for 2027, deliveries in 2028, and 85% of reservations are the range-extended Harvester trim.

item.title: Atlanta, Rivian, and the Quiet Coincidence
item.dc:creator: Jacob Hunka
item.description: Atlanta has a failing air quality grade and a Rivian plant on its doorstep. A hypothetical about what one city could do with the electric mobility infrastructure that already exists — R2 autonomous taxis, ALSO cargo quads, e-bikes, and ZTL-style restricted zones — and what the health data says the stakes actually are. Includes data from the HEI lockdown air quality study (Chen et al., 2025) and the American Lung Association's 2025 Atlanta air quality report.
